title: Tasteply: Externalizing Stable and Situational Preference as Manipulable Spatial Objects
abstract: arXiv:2611.07851v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Most recommender systems treat user preferences as a single signal to infer and optimize, yet human preferences are a mix of a stable preference and situational preferences that turn on and off depending on context. Through Tasteply, we externalize this preference structure as manipulable spatial objects. Tasteply represents each situational preference as an attractor and the stable preference as an underlying global field. Users can adjust their feed by moving around the space and adjusting the strength of the global field, turning the preference structure that remains latent within the model into something they can see and act on directly to steer the recommendation algorithm. Through an exploratory study (N=5), we found that this spatial control was effective, along with its limits and future direction as a means of manipulating preference-based recommendations.

translated_title: Tasteply：将稳定偏好与情境偏好外化为可操作的空间对象
translated_abstract: 大多数推荐系统将用户偏好视为单一信号进行推断和优化，然而人类偏好实际上是稳定偏好与情境偏好的混合体，其中情境偏好会根据情境的变化而开启或关闭。通过Tasteply，我们将这种偏好结构外化为可操作的空间对象。Tasteply将每个情境偏好表示为一个吸引子，将稳定偏好表示为底层的全局场。用户可以通过在空间中移动和调整全局场的强度来调整其信息流，将原本潜藏在模型内部的偏好结构转化为他们可以直接观察和操作的对象，从而引导推荐算法。通过一项探索性研究（N=5），我们发现这种空间控制方式是有效的，同时也揭示了其作为操纵基于偏好的推荐手段的局限性与未来发展方向。
tldr: 该论文提出Tasteply系统，将用户的稳定偏好与情境偏好这一偏好结构外化为可操作的空间对象，使用户能够直观地观察并操纵推荐算法的偏好。
en_tdlr: Tasteply externalizes the preference structure—stable preference as an underlying global field and situational preferences as attractors—into manipulable spatial objects, enabling users to directly see and steer preference-based recommendations.
